title: GTA 6 release date: Jason and Lucia start with small crimes
description: GTA 6 release date is November 19, and Jason and Lucia will reportedly start as small-time criminals, per Dexerto, with limits on cars and heists.

body.text: The GTA 6 release date is November 19, and a fresh report says the game will ease players in gradually. According to Dexerto, which cites The Guardian and Forbes, Jason and Lucia will start as small-time criminals and cannot pull off major crimes straight away. That matters because it changes how the first hours of the game will feel, especially for players used to causing chaos within minutes of starting a GTA title.
GTA 6 release date and what changes at launch

Dexerto says Grand Theft Auto VI is less than a week away from its worldwide launch. The soundtrack album also leaked on November 14, according to the publisher. It reportedly runs to 34 tracks across a four-side double album.
The new details are about progression. Players will reportedly have to work their way up before they try bigger heists, instead of jumping into the biggest scores right away.
Cars and break-ins are locked behind progression

Vehicle theft is the clearest example. Per the report, Jason and Lucia can initially only hotwire lower-end cars. More expensive rides, supercars included, stay off limits until players build more advanced abilities.
The same logic reportedly applies to getting into buildings. More sophisticated ways of breaking in will open up later in the game rather than being available from the start.

items: Early game: only lower-end cars can be hotwired.
Supercars: unavailable until players develop more advanced abilities.
Break-ins: more sophisticated methods arrive later.
Heists: require planning rather than a walk-in robbery.

body.text: Players also won't be able to simply turn up at a bank and take the cash, according to the report. They will need to scope out targets and think about security, including surveillance cameras and alarms.

That sounds like a more deliberate style of play. It rewards patience over speed, which fits a separate point in the Dexerto piece that GTA 6 pushes you to take your time with the main story instead of speedrunning it.

As per Forbes, Rockstar's Rob Nelson said the changes are partly meant to support the story. In his words: "Narratively, it doesn't make a lot of sense for them to go out and cause as much carnage and make as much noise as they can."
In other words, the limits are framed as part of the characters' journey, not just a gameplay gate. Dexerto also notes that GTA 6 is giving players more freedom to complete missions their own way.

These details come from reports relayed by Dexerto, so how restrictive the early game really feels will only be clear once players get hands-on after November 19. Watch for how quickly advanced abilities unlock, how much freedom missions allow, and whether the slower start suits both story fans and players who want instant chaos.

faqs.q: What is the GTA 6 release date?
faqs.a: According to Dexerto, Grand Theft Auto VI releases worldwide on November 19, less than a week after the article was published on November 14.

faqs.q: Can Jason and Lucia steal supercars at the start of GTA 6?
faqs.a: Reportedly not. Dexerto, citing The Guardian, says they can initially only hotwire lower-end cars, and supercars stay out of reach until players unlock more advanced abilities.

faqs.q: Why is Rockstar limiting crimes early in GTA 6?
faqs.a: As per Forbes, quoted by Dexerto, Rockstar's Rob Nelson said the changes partly support the story, since it doesn't make narrative sense for the pair to cause as much carnage and noise as they can.

sources.title: GTA 6 will reportedly restrict Jason and Lucia to small-time crimes at the start of the game
